algorithms.name: Saving a chapters version
steps: Take the proposed chapters, the author (manager or agent name), who asked (operator or none), the reason, and whether the save was asked for.
Every citation must resolve: Hub record ids against the project's tables, commit shas and tag names against the project's repository. Any that does not resolve refuses the whole version, naming it.

Every surface knot of the structural thread that existed when the previous version was saved must sit in exactly one chapter; a missing or doubled knot refuses the version, naming it. Knots recorded since may be placed or left ungrouped.

If the save was not asked for, compare each existing chapter with the proposal: any change to its title, summary or members is dropped and named in the result; only new chapters are kept. If nothing new is left, no version is written.
Write the version as a new row; never update or delete an earlier one.

algorithms.name: A chapters firing
steps: Skip if the job is off; skip an automatic trigger if the job is button-only.

Gather the structural surface (slice 1's feed), the current chapters with every earlier version and its reason, and, if no chapter yet covers the time before the first Hub record, a digest of the repository's history before it: release tags with their dates and the subjects of the commits between them.
Spawn the job's runner and model once with that input; record the firing with its usage whatever the outcome.
Save the answer through 'Saving a chapters version' with author manager, asked-for when the trigger was the button.

design:
Grounding (read, not run): manager jobs are a code registry (hub/hub/manager.py JOBS) with a per-project ManagerJob row (enabled, runner, model; db/models.py:1128); a sibling job is fired after a phase change with background.add_task (hub/hub/api/v1/spec.py:3075, vault_spec_check.check_in_background); firings are recorded as manager_job_fired with usage, and the Manager settings page already shows each firing's cost (hub/ui/src/components/settings/ManagerSettings.tsx:193) but no total. The thread feed is built in hub/hub/project_thread.py and served by hub/hub/api/v1/thread.py; slice 1's surface groups non-document knots with group_surface (:371).

The Hub enforces the rules, not the model: citations, every-knot-once and no-unasked-rewrite are checked when a version is saved, so a model that ignores its instructions changes nothing it was not allowed to.

Acceptance drive first: the acceptance-drive task writes scripts/drive/chapters_drive.py and shows it failing before the build; every other task depends on it, and drive-green runs it to pass.

Hazards: storing chapters needs a migration, and the operator's :8000 runs this checkout's migrations on its next restart. The ui task's committed bundle reaches their live app on reload. The first firing over 5,382 commits is the expensive one; its cost is shown, never capped.

Delivery: a flow, as slice 1. Developer builds; QA reviews and tests each finished task by driving the running product; every five minutes; stops when the queue empties. Tasks that share hub/hub/api/v1/thread.py are chained (feed, job, agent-tools).

open_questions.question: When does the manager rewrite chapters, and what may one firing cost? On major events and a 'Weave the thread' button; rewrites only when asked; no cost cap, the cost is shown and the operator controls whether it runs.
Which events are major? A document approved, a document archived, a document's last task approved.
What is beneath a chapter from before the Hub? Its commits, grouped by release.
A switch to hide chapters? No: once created they stay shown.
May chapters overlap in time? Yes.
Is version history shown to the operator? Not for now: agents and firings only.
The roadmap's done-condition contradicted 'chapters stay'. Reworded after the operator reopened it on 2026-10-23.
How is it built? A flow: Developer builds, QA reviews and tests, every five minutes, stopping when the queue empties.

problem: Slice 1's surface is one knot per specification document plus folds such as '12 items outside any document'. It is faithful but it isn't a story. On :8000 this project already has 159 documents (49 capabilities, 98 changes, 5 roadmaps, 7 system maps), all first recorded on 2026-10-22/23 because the corpus was imported then. The surface is therefore a list of document titles crowded onto two days, while seven months of work (from 2026-03-07) appear nowhere. A stakeholder can't tell from it what the project set out to do, in what order, or why.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-23: the manager decides what grouping best represents the work, whether by time, theme or roadmap; once chapters exist they stay shown.
requirements.statement: When a project has chapters, the Thread surface shows them ordered by when each begins, each with a title, a plain-language summary, its time span and who wrote it; opening a chapter shows, in place, the knots it groups. A project with no chapters shows slice 1's structural surface.
Chapters may overlap in time, so that two themes built in the same weeks are two chapters whose spans intersect.

requirements.rationale: Chapters are a reading of the history, not a filter on it; an item a chapter drops appears to the reader as if it never happened.
requirements.statement: Every surface knot of slice 1 belongs to exactly one chapter, so opening every chapter reaches the same items as the structural thread, none twice and none missing; a knot recorded after the latest chapter version appears after the chapters, ungrouped, until a later version places it. A chapter version that would drop or duplicate a knot is refused.

requirements.rationale: The roadmap's done-condition: chapters cite only real records. The page's promise is that nothing appears out of thin air.
requirements.statement: Every record a chapter cites (a stored Hub record, or a commit or tag in the project's repository) exists when the chapter is saved; a chapter version with any citation that does not resolve is refused and the previous version stays shown.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-23: this project's imported history is distilled from git, and its commits are shown grouped. Here that is 5,382 commits from 2026-03-07, 91 release tags and 221 dated archived openspec changes.
requirements.statement: For history earlier than the project's first Hub record, the manager writes chapters distilled from the project's git history, placed at the dates of the commits they cite and before every Hub-recorded knot. Opening one shows its commits grouped by the release tag they shipped in, each commit with its date, author and subject.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-23: these events are enough for now.
requirements.statement: With the chapters job enabled and automatic firing on, it fires after each major event in the project: a specification document approved, a document archived, or the last task of a document approved. It also fires whenever the operator presses 'Weave the thread' on the Thread page.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-23: a user who does not want this, or wants it done only by hand with a specific agent, must be able to say so.
requirements.statement: The operator can, per project: leave the chapters job off (the default), turn it on with automatic firing, or turn it on for the 'Weave the thread' button only; and choose which runner and model it uses. With the job off, the button is absent and nothing fires, and an agent the operator asks can still write chapters through its tools.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-23: no cost cap; control and visibility instead. The first firing over a long git history is the expensive one.
requirements.statement: Each chapters firing records what it cost (tokens and, where the runner reports it, money) and the operator can see the cost of each firing and the project's total for the job.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-23: rewriting is allowed but avoided unless the user asked, so the story a reader saw yesterday is still there today. The Hub enforces it rather than trusting the model to obey.
requirements.statement: A firing the operator did not ask for only adds chapters for knots no chapter yet holds; any change it proposes to an existing chapter is refused and the existing chapter stays as it was. Existing chapters are rewritten only by a firing the operator asked for, or by an agent a user asked to.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-23: future runs must know how the thread changed. Shown to agents only, for now.
requirements.statement: Every change to a project's chapters is kept as a new version recording who made it (the manager or a named agent), who asked for it when anyone did, when, and why; no earlier version is lost, and each firing and each agent reading chapters is given the earlier versions and their reasons.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-23: a user can ask an agent to organise the view as they like, using git commits or anything else the agent can read.
requirements.statement: An agent can read a project's chapters and their versions, and can create, retitle, resummarise, regroup or remove chapters through its tools; each edit is subject to citations-resolve and every-knot-once, and is recorded as a version under the agent's name.

in_scope: A manager job that writes chapters for one project's thread, grouping as it judges best
Chapters before the Hub's first record, distilled from the project's git history
Firing on major AgentWeave events and on a 'Weave the thread' button on the Thread page
Agent tools to read and edit chapters, used when a user asks an agent to organise the view
A kept history of every version of the chapters, readable by agents and later firings
User control over whether and how chapters are written, and visibility of what each firing cost
non_goals: A cost cap or budget on the chapters job (operator, 2026-10-23: control and visibility instead)
Recording any history the Hub does not record today, other than reading git (slice history-gaps)
Acting on work from the thread
Editing chapters by hand in the app (an agent edits them on the user's behalf)
Showing chapter versions to the operator in the app (agents and firings only, for now)
A switch that hides chapters once they exist

summary: The Thread tab's surface reads as a story. A manager job groups the project's history into titled chapters with plain-language summaries, each citing only records that exist, and reaches back before the Hub's first record through the project's git history. It fires on major events and on a 'Weave the thread' button. It may add new chapters on its own, but rewrites existing ones only when asked. Agents can edit chapters through their tools when a user asks them to. Every change is kept as a version. The user decides whether it runs automatically, manually or not at all, and sees what each run cost.
